summary: A blog post by Mike Rosa for Anabolic Aliens (dated Sep 29, 2020) compares the health benefits of hot and cold showers across muscles, skin and hair, immune system, mental health and weight. It concludes that cold showers are generally preferable if choosing one, suggests combining hot and cold (ending cold), and advises keeping showers under 10 minutes. The page's navigation, login, country lists and footer boilerplate are ignored.
one_line: Anabolic Aliens blog post comparing claimed health benefits of hot versus cold showers for muscles, skin, immunity, mood and weight.
key_facts: The article is titled 'Hot Vs. Cold Showers Health Benefits | The Ultimate Guide!' and was written by Mike Rosa for Anabolic Aliens on Sep 29, 2020.
The article states that hot showers are great for relieving tension and that cold showers can help speed up muscle recovery.
Cold showers are described as an ice pack that reduces muscular swelling or inflammation after workouts.
The article recommends hot showers as a pre-workout tension reliever and cold showers as a post-workout recovery tool.
For skin, the article says cold water hydrates the skin and closes pores, while hot water acts like an exfoliator by opening pores.
The article says hot showers can lead directly to dry skin, and that long hot showers can hurt skin and hair health.
For immunity, the article claims hot showers are well known for decongestant effects, loosening phlegm and easing sinus pressure.
The article claims cold showers have been proven to strengthen the immune system by increasing lymphatic movement.
For mental health, the article claims cold showers may relieve depression by igniting the serotonin neurotransmitter and releasing noradrenalin.
The article claims hot showers stimulate the brain to release more oxytocin, which significantly eases anxiety.
On weight, the article states that brown fat is more optimally activated by cold showers, increasing calories burned.
The bottom line says cold showers are more than likely the way to go if choosing just one, and recommends starting with 3 minutes of hot shower and ending with 5 minutes of cold shower.
The article advises keeping showers to under 10 minutes to save water.
The article's closing advertises an Anabolic Aliens membership offering workout classes, rehab programs and diet plans.
